data.name: Robonauts
data.detailed_description:
The beloved game that was originally released only for the Nintendo Switch console is coming to PC gamers now! Learn the story of Robo and help him save the galaxy, alone or together with family and friends.

Welcome interplanetary traveler!

In a nutshell, Robonauts is that arcade game which includes 12 levels. Each level will challenge you. You will explore a universe which consists nearly 50 planets, facing Bosses and creatures and meeting powerful opponents bent on universal destruction.

Who will you be (literally)?

Robo is a little robot whose curiosity got the better of him and led to his sudden exit from the confines of his safe environment. Now little Robo is far from home, fighting for his life against a constant barrage of enemies.
When developing Robonauts, we chose to give Robo human traits based on our own emotional experience. Robo acts like you and I, and we sense his emotions when has to choose between sides in a battle, trying to figure out who the good guys are. Once you get to know him, it’s hard not to love Robo.

Universe!

While the game is very dynamic, you get to choose your tempo of gameplay. A lot of troubles await you on every planet. We have tried to fill Robo’s universe with enough graphically various worlds that everyone who plays can find a unique favorite to which they can return. The graphics in this game are truly spellbinding. And the color scheme makes the game enjoyable for both kids and the kid inside every adult who remembers what it was like to spend a day in the arcade.
We really wanted to recreate the experience of the best arcade games from our childhood, so to pass a level, you have to jump between mesmerizing planets and destroy every opponent that stands in your way. Really, there are no words to adequately describe the Robonaut universe.

Music - the best for last

Game soundtrack composer, Simon Viklund. Yes the same Simon Viklund who worked on PAYDAY series and Bionic Commando Rearmed!!! His music exemplifies the very essence of Robonauts – dynamic, retro, arcade-style, energizing. What Simon has created is not only music for our game, but also the perfect soundtrack to your life - if you're just like us, that is.



FEATURES:
- great for the whole family,
- solo and local co-op
- local versus mode
- 12 unique planetary systems,
- large variety of weapons and enemies,
- explosive art style and graphics,
- epic music composed by Simon Viklund,
- easy-to-learn yet challenging gameplay,
- 2 difficulty settings: casual and hard.

data.short_description: Shoot through storms of weird and funny creatures, jump between planets by switching gravity, and relive the childhood fun of your very first arcade shooters - alone or with a friend in co-op!

reviews.review:
Nope, nada, no. Gameplay mechanics are completely broken which removes all the fun factor once the levels start getting serious with enemies. Full explanation below.

Let me first say that I double dipped as I have this game on switch. I only ever played the first couple of levels on switch and said "oh this is cool" but soon after literally stopped using my switch completely, (I only ever played it in handheld mode, I don't have a screen for the dock), once I got into PC gaming.
The music is absolutely outstanding and driving, though no tracks ever really reach the heights of the ones on the first 2 levels, but, it's still all good stuff.
When I saw it for a measly $6 AUD I thought why not buy it again and play through it proper on my laptop. I am sure it will have a better frame rate and graphics too.
That, it did. It seems to have an uncapped frame rate and 4 GFX presets.
There is no window control, but it seems to be in a windowed full screen format, not exclusive full screen. You can NOT change any of that, you can NOT change resolution. It did look like it matched my screen's native 1440P but I am not truly sure to be honest.
Besides the lack of any serious resolution and windowing options,  the next thing that annoyed me were the controls (I play with an xbox one elite 2 controller here). They are not re mappable in any sense, and unlike the switch version you can NOT shoot with the X button (Y on Switch) like you can with the switch version. Your main shot is hard wired to left bumper or left trigger, and secondary shot to right trigger/bumper. This is backwards to me. I could make it work on the switch, as it also threw the Y and A (as in X and B on xbox) buttons into the mix.. What I did was shoot with the Y button, jump with B and then use the right trigger for the secondary shot. Using the left trigger for the primary shot will NEVER feel intuitive to me as a right hander and I think the developer must be left handed and just never realised there are people different to them!
Why remove the option of shooting with the face button? I don't get it.
In any case, I persevered, cranked up the music and played through the first few levels. It was fun, but something I started noticing was as of about level 6 when a lot more enemies were about, above, below and beside you, you literally have NO control of the direction of the shooting. It's all automatic. You just press the button!
This is what I mean by broken gameplay mechanics.

For example.. there are these nasty little critters that can remove your entire life bar in a second, starting level six.
I tried to get through level seven at least 10 times and I gave up and decided to return the game.
Why you ask? Cause I was literally standing right next to the critter, imagine him an inch to my right on the screen, and I was desperately trying to shoot him and the gun was shooting upwards and it just wouldn't shoot him! It was aiming at some creatures on a different planet (if you play the game you'll know what I mean by different planet) above me whilst the critter on my right mercilessly drained my life.
In level 7, you have to protect 3 machines. Yes, these are as bad as the escort type of missions we all hate. Why do developers purposely add the types of levels we, as gamers, do NOT like? I will never understand this.
But every time I was 99% there, I was literally just about to save the last machine EVERY TIME, that critter with the kill shot would jump next to me and drain my entire life bar in a second and that was it. After I repeated that 10 times in a row.. I said.. "this is no longer any kind of FUN". If a game is not FUN, there is zero incentive to play it. I tried to at least jump his shot but this critter mimics your jump and shoots you airborne. So please developers., tell me HOW AM I SUPPOSED TO KILL SOMETHING THAT IS LITERALLY RIGHT NEXT TO ME IF YOUR GAME WILL NOT ALLOW THE GUN TO SHOOT AT HIM?

The game relies entirely on AI aiming, and it is really really broken. I can only imagine how bad it would get in even harder levels down the track. And I said, I am not supporting this baloney, and I got it refunded. Believe me you would understand if you played it and there was literally enemies around you, killing you, that you couldn't aim at and shoot.. Even moving left and right to try trick the AI to start shooting to my right didn't work. LOL. Frustration and wanting to throw a controller at the screen is NOT FUN. Challenge is great, but not that kind of challenge where it's cheap death after cheap death (oh, and you get one life per level, that's it).

Dear developers, let me tell you how to fix this game.
You make aiming controlled with right stick, aka twin stick shooter, so it's up to the player what to shoot, and you make the primary shot AUTO shoot when right stick is aimed anywhere. Because we still need to jump. Next, you put jump on left or right button/trigger, USERS's choice., Secondary weapon goes on the opposite trigger.
Planet hopping on the left or right stick click, i.e. L3 or R3.
Done.
Suddenly a 1/10 game becomes and 8/10 game.

It's stylish, sounds wonderful, has a good variety of weapons, yet it's no fun.

Oh and lastly, there are little green monsters that revive your health. But you guessed it, they disappear from the screen in a few seconds and they run in the opposite direction, at the same speed as you LOL. I literally gave up chasing for health pickups cause all I'd be doing was chasing things that were running from me that I couldn't catch up to, then they'd just vanish. Pro tip: If you are dead set on playing this, only go for health pickups travelling towards you. 

It's not often I see a developer really go out of their way to make a game no fun to play, but they have done it admirably here. It's literally almost ZERO fun. This coming from an arcade/shooter/action game fanatic.
Yep, 1/10.
